newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian coal output forecast little changed.
newsitem.headline: Australian coal output forecast little changed.

text.p: Australia's official commodities forecaster on Tuesday estimated a 5.6 percent rise in Australian coal production to 214.3 million tonnes for the year to June 1998, little changed from its March outlook.
The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) predicted exports of coal of 175.2 million tonnes, up 7.9 percent from 1996/97.

Most of the gain would appear in exports of thermal coal, for power generation, which would grow by 11.8 percent to 75.8 million tonnes, the bureau said. Output of metallurgical coal, for steelmaking, would grow 4.6 percent to 81.5 million tonnes.

The overall rise in export volumes, 7.9 percent, would more than offset a fall in prices and the bureau projected export income from coal to rise to more than A$8.2 billion in 1997/98 compared with A$7.9 billion previously.
Coal is Australia's biggest export commodity and outranks all other exports unless the various categories of tourism revenue are treated collectively.
ABARE said the outlook for next year's round of price negotiations with thermal coal buyers was improving.

"Background market conditions which may be conducive to firmer prices next year include some tightening in the spot market in the first half of 1997 and projections of substantial growth in demand in 1998 arising from the commissioning of a number of new coal fired power stations across Asia," it said.

The bureau also saw some signs that metallurgical coal prices would firm in the next negotiating round, although it said there were some risks for lower prices, particularly the use of poorer grades of coal in some coke blends.
